A dose‑response curve shows how the magnitude of a biological or physiological response changes as the amount (dose) of a stimulus—such as a drug, toxin, or environmental factor—is varied across a range. Typically the response rises at low doses, then plateaus or falls at higher doses because receptors become saturated, cellular pathways reach functional limits, or adverse effects dominate. Hence the curve can peak at an intermediate dose when the beneficial effect diminishes while saturating or harmful responses take over.
